- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.3) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to avoid overcorrection.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive downward moves), model should not overshoot upward; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent low.  
- After a sharp spike in sentiment (e.g., >0.2), forecast should not immediately revert to prior levels — allow 1–2 day lag to reflect market momentum.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true price by >3% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive, forecast should align with recent 7-day average, not 30-day trend.  
- Avoid forecasting upward when sentiment is negative and price is near 30-day low — model should wait for sentiment to turn positive before initiating upward moves.
